newsitem.title: GERMANY: NCA rules out short-term ex-Japan cargo rates chan.
newsitem.headline: NCA rules out short-term ex-Japan cargo rates chan.

text.p: Nippon Cargo Airlines said it has no short-term plans for any ex-Japan cargo rates rises or cuts.
Eiji Tanaka, NCA vice-president sales and marketing, told Reuters: "We do not want to change our rates.
"NCA is a first-class carrier and we want to maintain our current rates but we have worries about Kansai," he said.
Capacity now offered by Polar Air Cargo on its recently-launched all-freight flights from Kansai to the U.S. west coast was having a downward pressure on market rates, he explained.
Tanaka was speaking following the signing of a ground handling contract with Dutch trucking company Rutges BV at Frankfurt airport.
Asked about global air cargo market prospects for 1997, Tanaka said: "It will be a so-so year but I am optimistic. The US is still strong, Europe and south-east Asia are stable."
